title: Deploy FastAPI to Render (Free Tier)
description: Deploy a working FastAPI application to Render's free hosting platform with a PostgreSQL database and health check endpoint.
objective: Students will learn to deploy a FastAPI application to Render's free tier, connect it to a cloud PostgreSQL database, configure environment variables, and verify the deployment with a health check endpoint.

steps.title: Prepare the FastAPI Project
steps.instructions:
Before deploying, we need to make sure our FastAPI project has everything Render needs to build and run it.

**Step A:** Open your FastAPI project from Module 6 (or create a simple one). Make sure it has this folder structure:

```
techpath-api/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
├── requirements.txt
└── .gitignore
```

**Step B:** Add a health check endpoint to `app/main.py`. This is a simple route that tells Render "yes, my app is alive":

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI(title="TechPath API")

@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    return {
        "status": "healthy",
        "app": "TechPath API",
        "institute": "TechPath Institute, Bhopal"
    }

@app.get("/")
async def root():
    return {"message": "Welcome to TechPath API — built by students in Bhopal!"}
```

**Step C:** Make sure your `requirements.txt` has ALL dependencies:

```
fastapi==0.115.0
uvicorn[standard]==0.30.0
sqlalchemy==2.0.35
aiosqlite==0.20.0
alembic==1.13.0
python-dotenv==1.0.1
```

**Step D:** Create a `.gitignore` file to keep secrets and junk out of GitHub:

```
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.env
.env.local
venv/
*.db
```

**Checkpoint:** Run your app locally with `uvicorn app.main:app --reload` and visit `http://localhost:8000/health` — you should see the JSON response.

steps.title: Push Code to GitHub
steps.instructions:
Render deploys directly from GitHub, so your code needs to be in a GitHub repository.

**Step A:** Create a new repository on GitHub:
1. Go to [github.com](https://github.com) and sign in
2. Click the **+** button → **New repository**
3. Name it `techpath-api` (or any name you like)
4. Set it to **Public** (Render's free tier requires public repos)
5. Do NOT add a README (we already have code)
6. Click **Create repository**

**Step B:** Push your local code to GitHub:

```bash
# Navigate to your project folder
cd techpath-api

# Initialize Git (skip if already a git repo)
git init

# Add all files
git add .

# Create your first commit
git commit -m "Prepare FastAPI app for Render deployment"

# Connect to GitHub (replace with YOUR repo URL)
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/techpath-api.git

# Push to GitHub
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```

**Step C:** Verify on GitHub:
- Go to your repo on github.com
- You should see all your files: `app/main.py`, `requirements.txt`, `.gitignore`
- Make sure `.env` and `__pycache__/` are NOT there (the .gitignore should hide them)

**Checkpoint:** Your code is on GitHub and ready for Render to pick up.

steps.title: Deploy to Render
steps.instructions:
Now we connect GitHub to Render and deploy our app.

**Step A:** Sign up for Render:
1. Go to [render.com](https://render.com)
2. Click **Get Started for Free**
3. Sign up using your **GitHub account** (this makes connecting repos easier)

**Step B:** Create a new Web Service:
1. In the Render dashboard, click **New** → **Web Service**
2. Connect your GitHub account if prompted
3. Find and select your `techpath-api` repository
4. Click **Connect**

**Step C:** Configure the service settings:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Name** | `techpath-api` |
| **Region** | `Singapore` (closest to India) |
| **Branch** | `main` |
| **Runtime** | `Python 3` |
| **Build Command** | `pip install -r requirements.txt` |
| **Start Command** | `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` |
| **Instance Type** | `Free` |

**Important notes about the Start Command:**
- `--host 0.0.0.0` makes the app listen on all network interfaces (required!)
- `--port $PORT` uses the port number Render assigns (do NOT hardcode a port)

**Step D:** Click **Create Web Service**

Render will now:
1. Clone your code from GitHub
2. Run `pip install -r requirements.txt`
3. Start your app with uvicorn

This takes 2-5 minutes. Watch the build logs for any errors.

**Checkpoint:** Once the build finishes, you should see **"Your service is live"** with a green status. Your app URL will be something like `https://techpath-api.onrender.com`.

steps.title: Configure Environment Variables and Health Check
steps.instructions:
Now let us add environment variables and set up the health check so Render knows our app is running properly.

**Step A:** Add environment variables:
1. In your Render service dashboard, go to **Environment** tab
2. Click **Add Environment Variable**
3. Add these variables:

| Key | Value |
|-----|-------|
| `APP_ENV` | `production` |
| `DEBUG` | `false` |
| `SECRET_KEY` | Click **Generate** (Render creates a random secure string) |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | `*` (for testing; restrict later) |

4. Click **Save Changes** — Render will automatically redeploy with the new variables

**Step B:** Set up the health check:
1. In your service dashboard, go to **Settings** tab
2. Scroll down to **Health Check Path**
3. Enter: `/health`
4. Click **Save Changes**

Now Render will periodically call `https://your-app.onrender.com/health` to check if your app is alive. If it stops responding, Render will try to restart it.

**Step C:** Test your deployed app:

Open these URLs in your browser (replace with your actual Render URL):

```
https://techpath-api.onrender.com/           → Should show welcome message
https://techpath-api.onrender.com/health      → Should show health check JSON
https://techpath-api.onrender.com/docs        → Should show FastAPI Swagger docs
```

**Checkpoint:** All three URLs work. The `/health` endpoint returns `{"status": "healthy"}`. The Swagger docs page loads and you can test your API endpoints from the browser.

steps.title: Test Auto-Deploy and Verify
steps.instructions:
One of the best features of Render is auto-deploy — every time you push code to GitHub, Render automatically builds and deploys the new version.

**Step A:** Make a small change to your app. Open `app/main.py` and update the root endpoint:

```python
@app.get("/")
async def root():
    return {
        "message": "Welcome to TechPath API v2!",
        "institute": "TechPath Institute, Bhopal",
        "deployed_on": "Render (Free Tier)",
        "developer": "Built by Rahul during Module 15"
    }
```

**Step B:** Push the change to GitHub:

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Update root endpoint with deployment info"
git push origin main
```

**Step C:** Watch the auto-deploy:
1. Go to your Render dashboard
2. You should see a new deployment starting automatically
3. Wait for it to finish (1-2 minutes)
4. Visit your app URL — the root endpoint should show the updated message

**Step D:** Document your deployment. Take screenshots of:
1. Your Render dashboard showing the service running (green status)
2. The `/health` endpoint response in the browser
3. The Swagger docs page (`/docs`)
4. The deployment logs showing a successful build

**Final Checklist:**

| Item | Done? |
|------|-------|
| App is live on Render | |
| Health check endpoint works | |
| Environment variables are set | |
| Auto-deploy triggered on git push | |
| No secrets in GitHub code | |
| Swagger docs accessible at /docs | |

**Congratulations!** You have deployed your first app to the cloud. Share your live URL with your classmates at TechPath Institute!
